reason: The FAQ quote supports both five-level statements as attributed, but the qualifier 'not adjustable' (rendered for a limit) is not stated; note also the user guide says 'Excluding the root and AWS accounts', so the FAQ wording conflicts with it.
The quote states you can invite more than one account with a comma-separated list of email addresses or account IDs.
The quote states an administrator in the invited account must accept or reject via console, CLI or API.
The quote states the management account owner pays for all usage, data and resources of the accounts.
Under the accounts-count heading the FAQ says it can vary and to open a support case for an increase; the claim attributes this to the FAQ.
The quote states multiple accounts are a best practice for scaling, giving a billing boundary and isolating resources for security.
The quote states no Region is specified and a separate organization is needed for accounts used in China.
Under the heading asking about an organization without an SCP, the answer is yes, you decide which policies to enforce, with a consolidated-billing-only example.
The quote states an OU can be a member of only one OU at a time.
The quote states applicable policies such as SCPs are enforced automatically in the newly added account, with the root SCP example.
Under the heading about programmatic MFA on created accounts, the answer is 'No. This currently is not supported.'
The quote states an RCP can restrict access to identities in your organization or set conditions for external identities.
The quote states the free tier applies to total usage across all accounts in the organization, not to each account.
The quote states FullAWSAccess is attached to every root, OU and account when created and allows all services and actions; the context says it can be replaced.
Both quotes state that removing FullAWSAccess without a replacement blocks all actions below that level.
The quote states Organizations is a global service physically hosted in us-east-1.

The quota row supports 20 or the account maximum, whichever is greater, with accepted invitations not counting; the qualifier 'not adjustable' is not stated, and the page says some of these values can be increased.
The quote states each invitation must be responded to within 15 days or it expires.
The quota row states invitations count until declined, cancelled or expired, and closed accounts count until permanently closed.
The quotes state you can choose to create the role after acceptance and that Organizations did not create it automatically for invited accounts.
The quote, under a recommendation heading, says keep resources out of the management account because SCPs do not restrict its users or roles.

The quotes support consolidation of log data from all accounts and immutable, protected log data; the CloudTrail and AWS Config examples are only in the context, as a recommendation ('we recommend that you consolidate'), not in a quote.
The quote states you cannot change which account is the management account.
The quotes state the management account controls RI and Savings Plans sharing for any accounts, with account-level activate or deactivate.
The quote states the management account is the payer account and pays all charges of the accounts in its organization.
The quota row states 10 accounts, adjustable through Service Quotas, only the management account can request, and new organizations may be lower.
The quota row states increases can be granted up to 50,000 accounts based on customer qualifications and requirements.
The quote states a member account can belong to only one organization at a time.
The quote states created accounts must wait at least four days before migration and invited accounts are exempt.
The quote states you must wait at least seven days after the destination organization was created.
The quote states nested OUs inherit the parent OU's policies in addition to controls assigned directly.
The quote states no additional charge and that you pay only for resources used in member accounts.

The quota row gives a limit of 1 root, a maximum; 'exactly', 'fixed' and 'not adjustable' are not in the quote (add 'You can have only one root.' from orgs_getting-started_concepts, which also says the root is created automatically).
The quote states the trail logs all accounts, applies automatically, members can see but not modify or delete it, and by default cannot read its S3 log files.

The quote sits under 'Enabling trusted access with CloudTrail'; the same Organizations guide (organizations-userguide line 19289) says 'A user in a management account or delegated administrator account can create an organization trail', so the claim is broader than the quote supports.
The quote states an organization is a collection of accounts in a tree with a root at the top and OUs nested under it.
The quote states an OU is a group of accounts and can contain other OUs to form a hierarchy.
The quota row supports five levels of OUs under a root; the qualifier 'not adjustable' is not stated, and the page says some of these values can be increased.
The three quotes state OUs administer accounts as one unit, accounts inherit an OU policy automatically, and accounts can move between OUs.

The quote supports isolating production under top-level workload OUs and basing OUs on controls, not reporting structure; the non-production OUs for development and test are only in the context, not in a quote.
